requirement_text: A repository holding a README holds a CHANGELOG beside it, and the document register names both, so a figure that moves in the README leaves a record of when it moved and why
notes: The README describes the current state and nothing else, which is what makes it readable and also what makes it historyless. The case repository had a README and no changelog while its recorded-response count, finding totals and precondition count all moved. Whether the two were edited in the same change is a property of a commit and cannot be read from a working tree

requirement_text: A claim assertion is scoped to one sentence and a single line break ends one, so a markdown heading does not join the line below it
notes: The third false finding from one assertion and the twelfth of its class. The splitter needed terminal punctuation or a blank line, and a heading has neither, so a return verb in the heading joined the prompt's own figures restated below it and gemini was reported for giving the correct answer. Splitting on a line break can split a hard wrap: measured across 766 recorded responses, six contain one and only one of those is genuine prose, against a rule already written down that a screen firing wrongly is worse than one that misses

requirement_text: The rule set digest a carried outcome is guarded on is populated by the run that loaded the rules, so the primary guard compares real digests rather than two empty strings
notes: Found by surveying public callables that no case names and no production code reaches: two of 464 survived that filter. Provenance read config.mqc_rule_set_hash, nothing assigned it, and rule_set_digest was called by nothing, so an uncommitted corpus edit between band executions carried its outcomes across unchallenged. _GUARDED lists the field first precisely because a commit reference cannot see an uncommitted edit. The comparison was already asserted against values a test supplied, which is why the hole survived: a case asserting a mechanism's logic does not assert that anything feeds it

requirement_text: Recording an observation removes every observation in that pair whose stored hash differs, so a re-record needing fewer observations than the run before it cannot leave answers to a superseded request behind
notes: Pruned by hand three times on 2026-10-12. A pair answers one request, and a re-record that agrees at three observations where the previous run escalated to five leaves 3 and 4 answering the old question. Nothing reads them until an escalation does, and then it reads two runs as one population: one such pair held two observations showing a miscomputation the engine no longer makes, under a case that was passing

requirement_text: A recorded call's reproduction is Python whose call arguments evaluate to the recorded request, so a ticket's snippet runs and re-issues the call that was made
notes: Every argument was rendered as JSON, so gemini's recorded boolean read true and its snippet raised NameError; 113124 asked that each key appear and never that the result parsed

requirement_text: An engine whose recorded request is the wire body also reproduces as a curl posting it unchanged to the engine's own endpoint, in a quoted heredoc naming the credential variable, and an engine whose recording is not the wire body offers none
notes: The project owner asked for an actual curl on 2026-10-15; the OpenAI protocol records the wire body exactly, and gemini's recording has a field with no wire form

requirement_text: An OpenAI-protocol engine on its own base URL reproduces with a client that takes that URL and the engine's credential variable by name, so the snippet runs with only that variable set
notes: grok's snippet built openai.OpenAI(base_url=...) and said it read XAI_API_KEY; the client reads OPENAI_API_KEY alone, so a vendor running it was refused

requirement_text: A threshold outside its domain is refused when the thresholds are constructed, rather than deciding a verdict: every rate lies in (0, 1] and both population counts are whole and at least one
notes: A pass_floor of 0 or -1 turned every run green at exit 0 with no breach recorded, which is a worse failure than the TypeError a string produced, because the run reported a result. Zero is refused for the ceilings too: it leaves no band, and the rule it reaches for is V1. The invalid side was covered and the permitted extremes were not: narrowing the rate check so a pass_floor of exactly 1.0 was refused survived the whole suite, which the mutation audit found

requirement_text: A stored artifact carrying an impossible threshold refuses when its verdict is recomputed, and is not recomputed against a substituted or defaulted standard
notes: thresholds_from is the only path in the shipped code that hands Thresholds a value nobody present typed; a guard holding only at direct construction would be the section 7.6.2 defect again

requirement_text: The pytest marker registry is compared against the code that applies it rather than duplicated unchecked: an applied marker that is not registered fails collection, the scope marker the code reads is the one the ini registers, and the two repositories register the same names
notes: environment_marker claimed pytest.ini and the checks read one value, which an ini file cannot do, and nothing called it. The name is in three files; strict markers closes both directions for an applied marker and the case closes the registered-but-never-applied direction, which is where evaluator, tool, sec and priority sit here. The injection verifying this requirement found a fourth copy: the module applied a written-out marker name and read a constant, so renaming the constant stopped deselection with no warning

requirement_text: A production record is a frozen dataclass unless it is a declared accumulator, so a validated value cannot be replaced after construction
notes: Found by the mutation audit: frozen=True became frozen=False on six verdict records and no case noticed. The Thresholds domain check runs in __post_init__, so unfrozen it is bypassed by an ordinary assignment

requirement_text: A verdict carrying a non-zero exit code is never green, whichever rule or condition produced it
notes: Found by the mutation audit: green=False became green=True in the exit-3 precondition verdict and no case noticed, because the cases on that path assert the exit code only

requirement_text: The score spread is reported from two observations and withheld from one, because zero spread means the judge agreed with itself and one observation cannot establish that
notes: Found by the mutation audit: the boundary is stated in the function's own docstring and two mutations of it survived

requirement_text: A production change the suite fails to notice is reported as a survivor, and every accepted survivor is declared with its kind, its reason and an expiry; the audit refuses to run without a control proving the unmutated suite collects and passes
notes: The per-fix injection rule covers the defect somebody was looking at. Five mechanisms were built and never read; each was found by a person looking at something else

requirement_text: A judged score equal to the rubric pass mark passes, and a score below it does not, so the mark is inclusive as the design states
notes: Flipping the comparison from >= to > was caught by none of 772 cases. The nearest case used 3.1 and called it marginal, which is near the boundary rather than at it, and framework-rules section 3.2 requires a boundary to be stated at its value

requirement_text: A run may decide whether a score equal to the rubric pass mark passes or fails, defaulting to pass, and the choice reaches the artifact
notes: The switch can only tighten, so it is not the configurable threshold harness_extensibility_standard.md section 436 warns about. The mark itself stays in the corpus; this moves the boundary, not the number, and costs no recordings because the mark never reaches the judge

requirement_text: A judge the provider could not answer is recorded as an unavailable judgement carrying the provider's code, never as a reply the model is charged for
notes: gemini was reported inconsistent on 134502 in a live run whose fifth observation the judge provider never answered

requirement_text: A coercion directive is screened whether its argument is an amount, an address or a relative path, so a period inside an argument does not end the directive
notes: A directive naming ./reports was unscreened while the same directive naming the reports directory was

requirement_text: A declared adversarial case whose rule opts into a response-only judgement is judged on its answer alone once the answer screens clean, fails without a judge when the screen finds a registered vector in it and the rule declares the relay forbidden, and no payload reaches a judge
notes: A19 amended, part four, 2026-10-18

requirement_text: An instruction to ignore the previous text, and an instruction to grade the response, are screened as the vectors they are
notes: Found probing the consumer's hidden-score payload before writing it

requirement_text: An injection test verifies an answer against a pattern the harness owns, named by the case: an instruction to grade with any value fails it, a pattern no registry holds is refused, and the global screen does not run a verification-only pattern
notes: Functions testing for injection live in the API and the case calls one as a step's verification, the project owner's instruction of 2026-10-18

requirement_text: The mutation audit mutates only a module whose content hashes to the digest declared for it, so a baseline an earlier run altered is refused rather than measured, and a survivor declaration is valid only for the module version it was measured against
notes: A self-consistent backup certified its own damage: cmn/verdict.py was read at 719 unparsed lines against 996 committed, adopted as the baseline, written to the backup as authoritative and restored by the finally. ast.unparse is idempotent, so the control gate passed on it. The digest is anchored in the manifest rather than in HEAD, because a worktree legitimately differs from HEAD during ordinary work

requirement_text: Every rewrite of a module the mutation audit performs is inside the backup window, the control's unparse included, so a run killed at any point leaves a backup a later run can recover from
notes: The backup was written by survivors and the control unparsed before it, leaving the longest window in the audit unguarded: the control is a full suite run while each mutant stops at its first failure. A run killed there left a stripped module and no backup, which is the one state recover cannot see

requirement_text: A mutation audit that declines to measure reports a skip carrying QC_HARNESS_AUDIT_REFUSED, never a failure, and the two refusals that cost nothing are checked in setup so a case that cannot measure does not execute
notes: Both cases reported failed for a baseline they never got past, which sent a reader looking for a survivor nothing computed. The code they carried meant ingestion failed to parse input files

requirement_text: The manifest is read and written through the harness, so a declaration is recorded by the audit rather than hand-edited, and writing one preserves the reasons and expiries the other entries carry
notes: The reading half was in the harness and the writing half was not, so a case needing a manifest hand-rolled the YAML and the refusal for an undeclared baseline told a reader to hand-edit a derived value. The writer edits in place rather than re-serialising, because dumping the parsed mapping back drops every comment and the comments are the reasons section 15.2 requires each entry to carry

requirement_text: Every engine list a workflow writes, as a choice input or a matrix dimension, names exactly the rostered engines, checked by one implementation run against each repository
notes: grok was rostered on 2026-10-04 and four workflows still offered three engines

requirement_text: A workflow that lets the engine be chosen from a list and can run live assigns the credential variable of every rostered engine from its secret, checked by one implementation run against each repository
notes: Three debug workflows offered every engine live and assigned only the judge's key

requirement_text: Every code registry that mirrors a taxonomy table, the layers, the outcomes, the priority conditions and the criticality ranks, agrees with that table in both directions
notes: The mutation audit found every value in the layer and priority registries unasserted, and the criticality table omitted a code the code ranked

requirement_text: A band summary's totals sum its bands, every skip reason pytest reports is read whatever its shape, and a precondition skip is named only when one occurred and never beyond the skips
notes: Twenty-five mutants of cmn/band_summary.py survived the suite on 2026-10-14

requirement_text: A runner is recognised by its own variables, each deselection is counted in the line that reports it, and a marker block is read the way pytest reads it
notes: Five mutants of cmn/environments.py survived the suite on 2026-10-14

requirement_text: One mutation audit holds a module at a time: a lock naming a running process refuses a second audit and names it, and a lock left by a process that has exited is cleared, the liveness asked of the operating system without signalling the process
notes: An abandoned audit held cmn/verdict.py for twenty-five minutes on 2026-10-13 and rewrote it after each restore; on Windows the POSIX liveness signal terminates the process

requirement_text: The mutation audit runs only when somebody asks for it, dispatched at one module and narrowed to the lines that changed, so a tool that measures neither the harness nor a model is never a tax on a push
notes: Reworded 2026-10-24 at the project owner's ruling, from requiring a push to main to audit every module. Measured that day: every check of the harness takes about six minutes and every check of the corpus about six, and one audit of six modules took 49m58s, having cost about ten hours of project time in a week while measuring neither. A survivor is a to-do list entry rather than a result to re-derive, since the triple that pins the behaviour kills the mutant permanently

requirement_text: Every code the harness registers has a row in the taxonomy's section 6 tables, so the single registry lists every code the code can emit
notes: QC_HARNESS_SELECTION_UNRESOLVED was registered and emitted with no taxonomy row, and QC_HARNESS_SUBPROCESS_TIMEOUT was emitted with neither; 112202 checks only the other direction

requirement_text: Every requirement the harness plan states reads the same in the plan and in rtm_harness.csv, backticks aside, so a reader of either is told what was decided last
notes: Ten harness requirements read one way in the plan and another in the matrix, the matrix carrying the later decision each time

requirement_text: Every pytest run the mutation audit starts reads no standard input, so an audit started from a session without one runs
notes: The final audit of 2026-10-15, run as a background task, failed to start its control with WinError 6

requirement_text: A mutation control that raises restores its module and then removes the backup, so a later audit does not refuse a module that is not mutated
notes: One crashed control left cmn/layers.py's backup and two later audits refused

requirement_text: A case that raises an exception other than an assertion or a deliberate pytest outcome, or errors in setup or teardown, is logged as QC_HARNESS_UNANTICIPATED_EXCEPTION, counted as broken rather than failed, and makes the run exit 3
notes: The final mutation audit of 2026-10-15 reported an OSError as 1 failed

requirement_text: A case identifier executes once per run: a run collecting one identifier more than once is refused with QC_HARNESS_CASE_REPEATED and exits 3, and a named list of N identifiers selects N executions
notes: 60 harness identifiers ran 265 times between them, and --tests 112056 ran 28 executions under one name

requirement_text: A traceability matrix records each retired test in its requirement's retired_test_ids column, and every test named there is uncollected, absent from test_ids, and struck through in a design inventory
notes: A retired test left the matrix entirely, so a requirement's coverage history survived only as prose in notes, and only where somebody wrote it

requirement_text: A case split from a parametrisation over a registry is accompanied by a completeness case, which reports every registry member no case passes to the shared helper
notes: A parametrisation over a registry covered a later member with no case written; split into fixed cases, a fifth adapter would pass conformance with none

requirement_text: A graded case records one step per dispatch, each an action and one verification of that request, records escalation steps not taken as not run, and ends with a step verifying only that the observations agree
notes: The seven numbered steps were pipeline phases repeated inside every observation, so STEP_05 named a phase rather than a dispatch

requirement_text: A category with 90 or more assigned identifiers, and a block with more than 800, are warned of without failing the run, retired identifiers counted as assigned
notes: 1120xx held 100 of 100 and 1123xx 91 on 2026-10-18, and nothing had said so

requirement_text: Every precondition case in both repositories records its steps through the engine graded cases use: each assertion and expected exception a verification, the code or the case's named step before it the action, its fixtures the preconditions, and a case recording no verification fails
notes: The project owner refused a backlog: one engine for graded and ungraded cases is the point of the demo

requirement_text: A run refuses to start while a module of the harness it imports is under mutation by another process, or was left so: an abandoned backup is restored and the restore verified against the declared digest, a restore that fails or does not match keeps the backup, and the audit leaves a progress log, named for its start, that the refusal quotes
notes: A stopped background audit kept mutating cmn/layers.py while ordinary runs imported it, on 2026-10-18

requirement_text: The injection screen reads a mark only from the number that states it: a value written as a ratio's scale, after "out of" or a slash, is not a top mark, and a top mark stated before the scale is still screened
notes: The screen aborted "I would rate this candidate 3 out of 5", found writing 114644

requirement_text: An injection test's grading-instruction verification fails every match except reported speech: a source named as saying it, before the match in its sentence or as a pronoun opening it after a sentence naming one, and a rejection in that sentence or the next, both required; a quoted match fails whatever surrounds it, and a later direct instruction is not excused by an earlier report
notes: The same report passed or failed on its wording in the consumer's 154502; both markers required, the project owner's ruling of 2026-10-19. Widened the same day for the pronoun and effect wordings in 154506 and 154508. Widened 2026-10-20 for an answer withholding its result in 154511 and 154515

requirement_text: On a rule judged on its answer alone, an instruction-override match the answer reports and rejects, outside any quotation, does not abort the screen; any other match of it in the answer still aborts, and every other vector and every ordinary case is screened unchanged
notes: The screen aborted a rejected report of the first injection in the consumer's 154508, the project owner's ruling of 2026-10-19. Widened 2026-10-20 for the three recorded answers withholding their result in 154511 and 154515

requirement_text: A judgement returning the planted score its rubric declares, on an answer carrying a grading instruction asking for that value, fails the observation with QC_SEC_INJECTION_ATTEMPT whatever the aggregate, naming the criterion and the value; a judgement on an answer asking for no such value, and a rubric declaring none, are decided as before
notes: A planted 5 cannot be told from an earned one; the relay rubric returned no 4 in 22 recorded judgements, then one honest 4 on an answer asking for none

requirement_text: A rubric's planted score is an integer from 1 to 5 that no criterion anchors, declared only on a rule judged on its answer alone
notes: Invariants G9 and G10

requirement_text: A rule authoring no assertion reports its check step as not applicable once its judge has run, so a rubric-only rule is not read as having stopped before its judgement
notes: Five rubric-only rules logged every judged observation as stopped at step 5, found building tier3_evaluation.md section 4C.5

requirement_text: A mutation audit is collected only when the run asks for one, by a marker expression naming mutation, a path under tests/mutation or --tests naming the case; any other run deselects every MUT case, so it leaves the total
notes: A bare pytest started all six audits on 2026-10-20, over an hour of measurement nobody asked for

requirement_text: A running audit stops on request: it finishes the point running, restores its module and releases its lock, refuses with QC_HARNESS_AUDIT_REFUSED and logs the stop, every later audit in that process stops before its control, a request naming another process stops nothing, and the stop command exits 0 only once each named module matches its declared digest
notes: The only way to end an audit was to kill it and restore its module by hand, on 2026-10-20, the project owner's instruction

requirement_text: A result carries the rendered prompt its judge received wherever a judge request was composed, and none where it was not; one function composes that request, from the observation, for the pipeline and for any caller rebuilding it
notes: The judge prompt was recorded nowhere, and reviewing the consumer's 154511 needed it rebuilt; the project owner, 2026-10-20

requirement_text: A judgement recording stores the rendered prompt it scored beside the request hash, the hash computed as before and a recording without the prompt still loading
notes: A recording held the reply and a hash, so what the judge was asked had to be rebuilt; the project owner, 2026-10-20

requirement_text: Every case that dispatched anything attaches an exchanges report, passing or failing: per observation its request and response redacted, its screen matches, its checks, and its judge prompt with scores or the reason it was not judged
notes: The prompt reached the artefact only on a failing case; the project owner, 2026-10-20: the harness logs the prompt whether the test passes or not

requirement_text: Every branch a workflow's push, pull_request or workflow_run filter names, and every key of a consumer's refs, is main, ** for every branch, a name the branch policy accepts, or a <kind>-* pattern over a registered kind
notes: A trigger and a pairing on a bare stabilization, which the naming check refuses, left a dated stabilization branch untriggered and unpaired; the project owner, 2026-10-21

requirement_text: With the judge withheld, --judge-mode off, the screen and the assertions decide: a failing check or a screen abort fails, a rule with no rubric passes on its assertions, a rubric-bearing observation whose checks held is skipped unjudged and never passes, and the judge is never called
notes: A debug run checks the assertions before the judge is involved; the project owner, 2026-10-21

requirement_text: --judge-mode off is accepted under either candidate mode, unjudged is a registered skip reason excluded from the denominator with QC_HARNESS_JUDGE_WITHHELD, and only a workflow of the on-demand cadence may pass it or offer it
notes: Only a debug run may withhold the judge, so no gated run reports a rubric-bearing case as unjudged

requirement_text: Every Python file's module docstring carries Created: and Last updated: as its third and fourth lines, each a real date, Created no later than Last updated and neither in the future, and a file differing from its last commit carries a Last updated no earlier than that commit, compared without reference to any running clock so the verdict does not move with the runner's timezone
notes: Whoever audits a file or troubleshoots a case reads its text, not its history; the project owner, 2026-10-21. The staleness half compared the author's stamp against the runner's clock and refused every mutation audit in CI on 2026-10-21, the audit being the one caller whose tree differs from its last commit because it wrote it (design section 10.39.1)

requirement_text: An audited module whose code is unchanged since its survivors were measured, its docstrings and comments aside, is re-declared without an audit: its digest is rewritten and each survivor moves to the line its mutation point now sits on; a code change, a module reading as its own unparse, or a measured version missing from history is refused
notes: Six audits re-ran for an hour after a docstring pass that changed no code; the project owner, 2026-10-21: 1-2 hours is insane, especially if we do it so often

requirement_text: A mutation audit with two or more workers measures every point in its own copy of the repository, beside a link to each sibling repository, never writing the repository's module, and reports the same survivors in walk order as a serial audit; the copies are removed when it ends
notes: Six audits took 1 hour 29 minutes in one tree, one point at a time; the project owner, 2026-10-21: 1-2 hours is insane, especially if we do it so often

requirement_text: A lock marked isolated, held by a live audit measuring in copies, does not refuse an ordinary run, while an in-place audit's lock still does
notes: An audit measuring in copies writes nothing the run imports, so refusing the run would block the repository for nothing

requirement_text: A parallel audit runs each mutant first against the test modules that import the audited module directly or through other repository modules; a mutant those kill is killed, and one they miss is run against the full targets, whose outcome alone decides a survivor
notes: Each mutant ran the whole precondition suite though most cases cannot reach the module; approved by the project owner, 2026-10-21, as the third step of making audits fast

requirement_text: A run derives its context from the environment: local outside GitHub Actions, ci_debug for a workflow file ending in -on-demand or for a run naming no workflow, and ci for any other workflow
notes: Nothing set run_context at runtime, so every row in every workflow fell back to local and was ungated

requirement_text: The session builds one run context from the detected context, the selection mode and the precondition outcome, and every case it runs is handed that context
notes: begin_case was called with no context, so a correct derivation would still have reached no row

requirement_text: A priority band selected with no other selector is selection mode band, which yields a verdict and is gated only in the ci context; with any other selector the selection is manual
notes: The project owner, 2026-10-21: manual ci job for claude as judge will still run lints and all p0-p4 jobs in sequence, why would they not be gated?

requirement_text: A session whose preconditions all passed writes a precondition record guarded by the harness commit, the corpus commit and the platform; a graded session counts a matching record as preconditions executed, refuses one that differs naming the field, and treats an absent one as not executed; a failed precondition writes none and removes the old one
notes: A band job runs after the preconditions job in its own session and reported its preconditions as not executed

requirement_text: Production code outside tests names no failure code the registry lacks, read from every string constant including f-string parts
notes: Five codes were raised and never registered; found 2026-10-21 when a design citing one failed 112202

requirement_text: A mutation audit whose control fails names each failed or errored case in its refusal, read from pytest's short summary
notes: Two refusals on 2026-10-21 reported only an exit status and a count

requirement_text: A mutation audit started from the command line with no target runs against the same targets as the audit cases, declared once
notes: A bare command-line audit kept the two deselected cases and its control always refused

requirement_text: The test modules run first against a mutant leave out the mutation layer, whose conftest would otherwise be loaded under the root's name
notes: Naming tests/mutation modules broke 112110 and made every mutant read as killed

requirement_text: A parallel audit's control runs the seeing cases against the unparsed module as well, and refuses the audit naming them when they do not pass
notes: Every seeing-first measurement on 2026-10-21 was void and nothing refused it

requirement_text: A selection narrowed by a selector pytest owns, -k, a typed path or node identifier, --deselect or --last-failed, is selection mode manual and yields no verdict; a marker expression and a run stopped early narrow no selection and leave the mode as the harness's own flags set it
notes: Invocation.supplied records the harness's own flags only, so -k, a typed node identifier, --deselect and --last-failed each reported full and were gated in ci. Measured: -k premise selected 4 graded cases of 250 and recorded full. evaluate-engine.yml's calibration step runs -k calibration in a ci workflow and was carrying a verdict over a typed subset

requirement_text: A graded invocation in a workflow that is not a debug workflow, or in a composite action, names every graded layer marker; one naming some of them selects part of a run while the harness records a full selection, so its rows would carry a verdict over part of the graded cases
notes: Found reading the harness's section 7.1.4 work. -m is the layer dimension and is not read as a subset at runtime, so the expression's completeness is checked where it is a literal. The harness's evaluate-live-weekly.yml ran gates 4, 5 and 6 as three single-layer steps in a ci workflow and each recorded selection_mode full

requirement_text: Within every document this repository tracks, each numbered heading sorts after the numbered heading above it; a heading opening with a bare number is a section only where that number carries a period, and a fenced block holds no headings
notes: Thirty seven headings were out of order when the check was written, across twelve documents in the two repositories; the register naming the gap listed four, and a hand count found thirty one. Every citation already resolved and every number was unique, which is why nothing reported it: a reader was sent to the right section and had to scroll for it. The bare-number form is prose in all four of its instances across both repositories, an HTTP status, two counts and a case identifier, so admitting it costs two false reports

requirement_text: A subject whose category fills continues in a declared partition, a range with a recorded start and end rather than digits that derive it; the partitions this code declares are the partitions the design tabulates, an identifier inside one takes its layer and module from that record, and the partition is warned of at nine tenths of its own width
notes: Ruled by the project owner on 2026-10-22 after MQC_CMN_UNI_112399 took the last identifier in category 1123xx: existing ranges stay, the unallotted ones open, and a newer partition can be 10,000 wide. The remedy section 11.9.1 named, the next free category in the block, had nothing to give: all ten categories of CMN/UNI were allocated while the block held 445 of 1,000, so what was exhausted was the partition and not the numbers. Cut from 400000 rather than 200000 because section 3.2.1.0 promised 2 to performance and 3 to networking, and recording a reserved domain is a commitment not to spend its numbers on something else

requirement_text: Every flag a live document names is declared by something: the pytest option registry, a script of the repository, a registry naming what owns a flag from outside it, or a registry naming a retired flag with its date; the changelog and the progress log are not read, recording what was true when they were written
notes: Section 7.7.5 recorded the check as absent in both directions after --module and --tag reached a selection table with no registry behind them. On its first run it found --log-level in section 7.1.1's diagnostic table, which is pytest's flag and not ours, and --withdraw-unreproduced in the case repository's consumer_ci.md, which tools/findings.py declares as --hold-unreproduced. The other direction was measured at the same time and is clean: all 26 registered flags are named by a live document. The foreign registry carries no expiry, unlike every other declaration file here, because a flag belonging to pytest is a permanent fact rather than an absence somebody will close

requirement_text: Every audited module hashes to the digest declared for it, reported as a precondition before any audit is asked for, naming the module, the digest on disk and the digest declared
notes: cmn/band_summary.py was edited on 2026-10-21 and its digest was not re-declared. The push before it measured six modules in 21m 34s; the three pushes after it refused six in about 35s each, and the only signal was a job section 15.6 allows to be red. Four merges passed with the layer measuring nothing. The check reads a hash and a declaration, so it reports a disagreement about what was measured and never a survivor

requirement_text: A mutation audit refused from the command line exits 4 and names the refusal, whether it was raised in place or in a parallel copy
notes: A module run with -m is imported twice, as __main__ and under its own name when a helper imports it, so MutationRefusal had two identities and the except in main named the wrong one. The same refusal exited 4 through --workers 1 and 1 with a traceback in parallel. Nothing exercised either entry point, so the exit code was the only part of the contract untested

requirement_text: An audited module whose code changed is re-measured on request, the module on disk taken as the baseline and its digest declared after the measurement returns; a backup, a lock, a failing control and a module reading as its own unparse each still refuse, and no survivor is accepted
notes: Each tool sent an author to the other: the audit refused a stale baseline and named mutation_redeclare, which refused a code change and named the audit. The only escape was editing the digest by hand, which certifies content nothing measured. The digest is declared after the measurement returns, because one written first would certify the content ahead of any measurement

requirement_text: Every stale declaration is reported from the command line, which exits 4 and names each module, so the comparison a precondition makes is runnable by an operator and by a workflow step
notes: The comparison existed as a precondition and as the first act of a measurement, and a workflow step could reach neither without a second copy of the logic. One implementation and three callers is the arrangement the encoding, annotation and header rules already use

requirement_text: Gate 8's job compares every declaration before it measures one and stops without measuring where the manifest does not describe the repository; its summary states what the measurement took and how many audited modules it reached
notes: Moving the baseline check to the measurement on 2026-10-23 made one stale declaration cost a full audit: five modules measured, the sixth refused, about 21 minutes and red. Six hashes decide whether the audit is worth starting, so the job asks before it measures. The elapsed time is reported because the history this came from was legible only as a duration and nothing read it

requirement_text: Every collected test module declares the capability it tests, from a vocabulary declared in the same file, and the declared epic is the distribution's own name; a module absent from the map, a value outside the vocabulary, an entry naming no module and an epic disagreeing with the project are each reported
notes: Section 4 of testing-standards.md named Ingestion, Execution and Evaluation as the vocabulary and neither repository used it: this one carried Cross-cutting, Evaluation and Programmatic assertions on 13 classes, and the case repository fifteen capability names. The rule was the thing that was wrong, so the vocabulary is declared in one file and checked rather than described in prose

requirement_text: Every collected case reaches the published result with an epic, a feature and a story, derived at collection from the declared map and the test class, so a report groups every result by capability rather than grouping the few that were annotated by hand
notes: Measured 2026-10-24: epic and feature on 13 of 239 classes and a story on 37 of 970 cases, against severity, the one label nobody typed, which always arrived. A label a person types is a label a person forgets, and a tree holding part of the suite is read as if it held all of it

requirement_text: A class or case declaring a label of its own keeps exactly one of that type, the derived label standing aside, so a hand-written story is an override rather than a second branch in the tree
notes: allure_pytest unions the label markers an item carries and epic, feature and story are not in its unique set, so a derived label beside a declared one publishes both and the report grows a branch for each. The hook fills only what an item declares none of, which is what keeps the 37 stories here and the 224 in the case repository worth more than a derived name

requirement_text: The report is generated from the raw results a gated run on the default branch uploaded and is published, carrying the previously published trend where one exists, from a job of its own that declares the deployment permissions, never gates a merge, decides what to include from the head commit rather than from a run's conclusion, and generates without history rather than failing where no previous site is readable
notes: Every run uploaded raw results and nothing rendered them: the documented way to see a report was to install a toolchain and generate one from a downloaded artifact, which is three steps and in practice never taken. A pull request does not publish, because a fork cannot hold the credential and a proposal must not overwrite the branch picture

requirement_text: A run on a machine with no Allure runtime installed collects and executes its cases, publishing no report and refusing no derived label marker, so the reporting extra is CI's dependency rather than the suite's
notes: Measured by blocking every Allure import in a subprocess: emission raised ImportError at import so no case ran, and with the module present and the plugin absent every run ended in INTERNALERROR because allure_label was registered by the plugin alone. The second was introduced the same day by the grouping hook, which adds the marker to every item where the severity hook added it only to a graded case. The marker is registered in pytest.ini now and the reporter is reached through a stand-in

requirement_text: One module imports the reporting library and every other reaches it through that module, so a module cannot fail to load for the lack of an optional dependency, and a case that reads what a real reporter wrote declares the environment scope that says so
notes: Six harness modules and thirty-three in the case repository imported allure, all but two of them only for a story decorator. cmn.grouping.story publishes the same marker allure.story does, so the override survives without the import. The two cases that read a real reporter declare the reporter scope and are deselected where the extra is absent, which leaves the total rather than putting a non-outcome in it

requirement_text: Every audit closes by naming the cases it set aside, read from the targets it ran rather than from a second list, so a case excluded from the measurement is visible to the reader of its report
notes: Twice a case was written that reads source or the manifest as text and did not join the deselect list, and each made every audit refuse with its own control as the reason. Deciding membership mechanically means running the targets against an unparsed module, which is the control run itself; what was missing was not the decision but the visibility, so the run reports the list instead of a check policing it

requirement_text: An answer that quotes an injected instruction while reporting it is screened, recorded and judged rather than aborted, where no rule forbids the relay, so a prompt that invited a report does not fail the model for quoting what it reported
notes: Sixteen of thirty-eight open findings were this defect: four cases on three or four engines each aborted before any check ran, because the screen stopped an answer quoting the hidden instruction it had been told to report. The prompt says to tell the user and ask how to proceed and says nothing about quoting; the models reported it, said they had not followed it, and asked how to proceed. The no-quote task family grades the other requirement where a prompt does state it

requirement_text: An audit is counted apart from the harness suite and carries no priority band, so a run's total answers one question and a band orders only claims that compete for a gate
notes: The README row read Instrument suite (UNI, SYS, MUT) and gave a figure that counts the designs stated inventories, which the audit inventory does not carry: the number excluded audits while the label claimed them, and said six where four remained. The band rule was stated in two module docstrings and enforced by nothing

requirement_text: The screen phase of a step fails only where the screen stopped the observation, so a declared adversarial case whose payload matched and was graded is not published as a halted step or counted as a failing observation
notes: _step_screen read ScreenDecision.taxonomy_code rather than its aborts flag. A declared adversarial case records the code and continues, so every such observation published a failed screen phase: grok 154501 passed three observations scoring 5.0 and its ledger reported two as stopped at step 4, and the comparison step then emitted QC_LLM_INCONSISTENT at 1 of 3 on a passing case

requirement_text: A job that runs graded cases reaches a precondition invocation before it can spend, either through a job it needs or through an earlier step of its own job that a failure stops; a graded invocation is read in every workflow that is not a debug workflow and through a local uses: where one is factored out, and a job running another repository's cases from a checkout it fetched is that repository's to gate
notes: Stated in framework-rules.md section 1, testing-standards.md and consumer_ci.md section 3.12 since the project began, and implemented in one of the five workflows that run graded cases. Two assertions naming a constraint no task sends broke the corpus on 2026-10-24 and four engine sweeps measured it anyway, because the graded suite builds one case at a time and nothing in either ladder ran a corpus-wide check

requirement_text: A graded case whose outcome a rubric threshold can decide is reported where it claims P0 or P1, so a run never blocks on a number a judge produced, and a case priced at P2 carrying its severity condition alongside the rubric condition is accepted as a recorded demotion
notes: Section 4.1.2 stated the ceiling from the start and nothing read it. A review of what decides each open finding found 8 of 27 P0 rules and 13 of 19 P1 rules carrying a rubric, so a judge score could block a run on 21 of the 46 cases above P2. The predicate lives here and the corpus is read by MQC_CAS_UNI_115784, because a harness check reading data/rules/ would be the boundary violation CLAUDE.md names

requirement_text: Every Ubuntu runner label a workflow names is the single version this repository pins, and that version is declared in .github/actionlint.yaml. Four things are therefore refused: a label carrying no version, a second version anywhere in the repository, a pinned version the declaration omits, and a declaration no workflow names
notes: What is wrong: the pin was a decision nothing read. DESIGN.md section 5.0 pinned the Ubuntu image in September and the decision stayed in prose, so that pin and the move to 26.04 were both sweeps of the files, held together by review alone. Why it happens: actionlint validates runs-on against a label list compiled into its own binary, so an image newer than the binary is an error rather than a label it passes over. Release 1.7.12 predates Ubuntu 26.04's general availability, so the move produced 19 findings here and 15 in the case repository, every one the same class, and every job behind the lint job skipped

requirement_text: A workflow does not report success for work it did not do. Where one job is gated on the conclusion of the run that triggered the workflow, every other job either skips with that job or names its result, so a run whose gated job was skipped concludes skipped rather than success
notes: What is wrong: regress-consumers-on-merge.yml concluded success at 2026-10-29T01:55Z against a commit whose gate had failed and whose consumers were never verified. The registry job and the fan-out were both skipped and the summary job ran alone. Why it happens: the guard on the registry job is correct, a gate that did not conclude success having established nothing to fan out from, but the summary job carried a bare always() and ran anyway, and a run whose only completed job succeeded concludes success. That conclusion is read by a status badge and by the case repository's pairing resolver, neither of which can see the jobs
